methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Tech researchers look to AI to ease difficult workplace conversations
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech developing open AI training tools represents knowledge creation in non-NoVA regions with potential for broad distribution if the tools become accessible to workplaces statewide, signaling deep capability development outside traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: RiverStreet Networks removed from multiple broadband deployment projects in rural Virginia after years of delays
signals.signal_reading: Broadband infrastructure failure blocking 30,000+ rural connections creates a foundational barrier preventing both shallow platform adoption and deep AI capability development, reinforcing the concentration of digital capacity in already-connected metro regions.

signals.title: From AI cameras to drones, Fairfax Co. uses new technology in policing
signals.signal_reading: Fairfax County deploying advanced AI surveillance systems (cameras, drones) demonstrates deep technical implementation concentrated in well-resourced metro jurisdictions, widening the capability gap with rural localities lacking funds for sophisticated AI tools.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targeting community-wide AI education and innovation signals intentional distribution strategy in Richmond metro, potentially creating peer learning networks that spread deeper capability beyond elite institutions.

signals.title: SCC considers making data centers shoulder more of the cost of transmission lines
signals.signal_reading: SCC debate over data center transmission cost allocation reveals how AI infrastructure investment concentrates economic burden and benefit, with policy decisions determining whether rural Virginians subsidize NoVA's AI compute advantage or share in distributed gains.
